
QUERY-ORPHANS
Detect orphaned work units with no epic assignment or dependency relationships

WHEN TO USE
  Use this command to identify work units lacking context and traceability. Essential for work unit hygiene, preventing unplanned scope creep, and ensuring all work aligns with epics or has clear relationships. Run after bulk work unit creation or periodically for maintenance.

PREREQUISITES
  • spec/work-units.json exists with work units

USAGE
  fspec query-orphans [options]

OPTIONS
  --output <format>
    Output format: json or text
    Default: text
  --exclude-done
    Exclude work units in done status from orphan detection

COMMON PATTERNS
  • Maintenance Workflow
    Example: # Weekly cleanup: find orphans
fspec query-orphans

# Assign epics to valid work
fspec update-work-unit MISC-001 --epic=documentation
fspec update-work-unit REFAC-003 --epic=authentication

# Add relationships for cross-cutting work
fspec add-dependency MISC-001 --relates-to AUTH-001

# Delete invalid work units
fspec delete-work-unit INVALID-001

# Verify cleanup
fspec query-orphans
    undefined

  • Bulk Work Unit Validation
    Example: # After creating multiple work units
fspec create-story AUTH "Setup auth"
fspec create-story AUTH "Login flow"
fspec create-story AUTH "Logout flow"

# Check for orphans
fspec query-orphans

# Assign epic to all
fspec update-work-unit AUTH-001 --epic=authentication
fspec update-work-unit AUTH-002 --epic=authentication
fspec update-work-unit AUTH-003 --epic=authentication
    undefined

  • JSON Export for Reporting
    Example: # Export orphans for dashboard
fspec query-orphans --output json > orphans.json

# Count orphans by status
jq '[.orphans[].status] | group_by(.) | map({status: .[0], count: length})' orphans.json
    undefined


TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  1. Run orphan detection: fspec query-orphans → 2. Review orphaned work units → 3. Assign epic OR add relationship: fspec update-work-unit <id> --epic=<epic> OR fspec add-dependency <id> --relates-to=<other-id> → 4. Delete if invalid: fspec delete-work-unit <id> → 5. Verify: fspec query-orphans

EXAMPLES
  1. Find all orphaned work units (no epic, no relationships)
  $ fspec query-orphans
  Found 3 orphaned work unit(s):

1. MISC-001 - Update documentation (backlog)
   ⚠ No epic or dependency relationships
   Suggested actions:
     • Assign epic
     • Add relationship
     • Delete

2. REFAC-003 - Refactor auth module (implementing)
   ⚠ No epic or dependency relationships
   Suggested actions:
     • Assign epic
     • Add relationship
     • Delete

To fix orphaned work units:
  fspec update-work-unit <id> --epic=<epic-name>
  fspec add-dependency <id> --depends-on=<other-id>  (or --blocks, --relates-to)
  fspec delete-work-unit <id>

  2. Find orphans excluding completed work
  $ fspec query-orphans --exclude-done
  Found 1 orphaned work unit(s):

1. MISC-001 - Update documentation (backlog)
   ⚠ No epic or dependency relationships
   Suggested actions:
     • Assign epic
     • Add relationship
     • Delete

  3. Output orphans as JSON for automation
  $ fspec query-orphans --output json
  {
  "orphans": [
    {
      "id": "MISC-001",
      "title": "Update documentation",
      "status": "backlog",
      "suggestedActions": ["Assign epic", "Add relationship", "Delete"]
    }
  ]
}

  4. Count orphaned work units
  $ fspec query-orphans | wc -l
  15

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Error: No orphaned work units found
    Fix: All work units have epic or dependency relationships. No action needed.

  ✗ Error: work-units.json not found
    Fix: Run: fspec init to create work-units.json file

  ✗ Error: Invalid work-units.json format
    Fix: Check for JSON syntax errors in spec/work-units.json

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec query-bottlenecks
  fspec suggest-dependencies
  fspec update-work-unit
  fspec add-dependency
  fspec delete-work-unit
  fspec list-epics

NOTES
  • A work unit is orphaned if it has NEITHER epic NOR dependency relationships
  • Orphaned work units lack context and traceability (unclear WHY they exist)
  • By default, includes ALL statuses (even "done" work can be orphaned)
  • Use --exclude-done to focus on active work units needing attention
  • Orphans often indicate ad-hoc work added without proper planning
  • Suggested actions: (1) Assign epic, (2) Add relationship, (3) Delete if invalid
  • Regular orphan detection prevents unplanned scope creep
